title: Probe Factory Terraform module + upgrade-safe SLO checks for Private VPCs
creator: Marco Liu
description: Build a reusable Terraform 'probe-factory' module that provisions per-customer health probes and SLO checks for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should create latency, 5xx error-rate, token-throughput and saturation probes with sane defaults, support per-customer overrides, and be safe during control-plane and runtime upgrades (canary-aware, rollback hooks). Deliverables include the Terraform module, unit/integration tests, Grafana dashboards + default alerting rules, and a CI job that validates probe behavior against a synthetic load harness before upgrades are promoted.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published to internal registry at registry.terraform.io/redwood/probe-factory with semantic versioning
Module parameters allow per-customer thresholds (latency P95/P99, error rate %, token/sec capacity, queue depth) and fallback to platform defaults
Upgrade flow includes a canary release that runs synthetic probes against newly provisioned resources and gates rollout on no SLO regressions
Automated CI verifies probe creation, PromQL/Grafana queries return expected metrics in synthetic tests, and a rollback plan is executed automatically if thresholds exceeded
Comprehensive docs (usage, defaults, overrides, troubleshooting) published in docs.redwood.com and linked from Console's Private deployment page
comments: 2025-02-11 - Kickoff: scoped initial module interface with infra and observability. Decided to support two paths: lightweight managed probes (platform-managed alert blocks) and full customer overrides. Trade-off: more options increases surface area but reduces after-deploy edits.

2025-02-14 - Design note: use templated PrometheusRule resources for alerts + a small sidecar that validates token-throughput estimates against runtime metrics. Concluded this is less intrusive than changing runtime and keeps upgrade path simpler.

2025-02-20 - Implementation update: core TF module drafted in rw-terraform-modules/probe-factory. Initial variables: latency_p95_ms, latency_p99_ms, error_rate_pct, token_throughput_min, saturation_queue_threshold. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-terraform-modules/pull/812

2025-02-24 - Review feedback from Observability: prefer percentile-based alerting for latency windows, add short-window alert (1m) for burn spikes and long-window (1h) for trend detection. Also asked for clear runbook steps in alert annotations.

2025-02-26 - E2E test harness: lightweight synthetic generator (k6 script) added to validate token throughput and saturation under two profiles (steady and burst). CI job name: ci/probe-factory/e2e. Failing when synthetic P95 > configured threshold.

2025-03-01 - Security review requested. Item: ensure probe metadata does not leak customer identifiers in metric labels. Proposed solution: tag metrics with hashed_customer_id; security accepted the approach pending implementation.

2025-03-03 - Canary strategy: module now emits a 'canary-check' resource which CI applies to the canary stack. If canary exhibits >2% error-rate regression or >10% token throughput drop vs control, rollout is blocked and auto-rollback plan runs. Added terraform apply-time hook to annotate canary run with run_id.

2025-03-05 - Blocker noted: Terraform provider version mismatch in Dedicated customers' onboarding scripts causing PrometheusRule CRD schema drift. Suggested mitigation: pin provider in module and add migration docs. Assigned follow-up ENG-140999.

2025-03-05 - Next steps: finish provider pinning, add more synthetic scenarios (graceful degradation, KV-cache-warmup), finalize runbook, and schedule a staged rollout with two pilot customers in week of 2025-03-17.
